title: Mexican muralism
summary: In 1922 in Mexico City, state-sponsored mural painting took off under education secretary José Vasconcelos, who saw murals as a way for people to read their social reality. Roberto Montenegro painted the movement's first mural, El árbol de la vida; Diego Rivera painted the largest extent of mural work at the Secretaría de Educación Pública.

uncertainty.note: 1922 is the year of the first mural and of the founding date Memórica México cites; the movement continued for decades, so the end year here marks the founding, not the end of the movement.

as_recorded.value: desde finales de 1922, hecho que marca la fecha considerada fundacional del movimiento

where.historical_name: Mexico City, Mexico, after the Mexican Revolution

importance.justification: The SEP calls Mexican muralism the greatest expression of the cultural movement driven by Vasconcelos.

related.because: Memórica México says the mural program was meant to spread and promote the new ideals of the revolution in power.

sources.title: A un siglo del nacimiento del muralismo mexicano

reviewer_note: Memórica México counts the first mural and the late-1922 union announcement. Other publishers place the start at 1920 or 1921; those were not opened. Both opened sources are Mexican government publishers; an independent foreign source was not obtained (moma.org blocked fetches).
